Resolves #20614

The off-socket Neural Link adapter can now bind an exact App Worker UUID in a second browser context. Each page owns one worker binding, its captured logs and the navigation/last-window release hooks, so another connection cannot redirect an existing SDK. Names remain scoped to the fixture page. The two cold-boot Workstation spec files join the engine tier without a Brain checkout.

Related: #20615 (prerequisite, now merged).

Evidence: L3 (live off-socket Chromium journeys, plus L2 unit controls) → L3 required (local red/green and two hosted engine-tier runs). No deployment or appearance-acceptance claim.

## Contract Ledger

| Surface | Preserved or extended behavior | Owning evidence |
|---|---|---|
| `connectToApp(target)` | UUID selects the root page reporting that exact worker id across browser contexts; a name still addresses only the fixture page. The attached worker's ready id must also agree. | `dedicatedWorkerNeuralLink.spec.mjs`: closed fixture, root before popup, wrong-id refusal. |
| Returned `nlApp` | Worker getter and logs remain with its page even after another context connects. The same binder releases before main-frame navigation and when that context's last window closes. | Both adapter unit files; unchanged writer-lifetime consumer. |

## Deltas from ticket

- Factor the prerequisite's existing hooks into one page binder instead of copying them. Already-open sibling pages get the close hook as well as future pages.
- Update the existing writer-lifetime test's Page facade with `context()`, which a real Playwright Page provides. No writer-lifetime assertion is relaxed.
- The two spec files' run comments now show the off-socket command. No journey assertion or timeout changes.
- Change class: capability (`feat`). `agent-preflight` is not hosted in this Engine checkout; shared baseline and guards supply hosted checks.

## Test Evidence

- Base `8ff14e8ebd`: one cold-context arm from each file fails with the 30-second `connectToApp(workerId)` refusal; both also hit the existing 180-second teardown failure. The two dedicated-worker regression arms fail on that same unchanged adapter; the wrong-id control passes.
- Candidate locally: both complete Workstation files pass off-socket through the standard E2E config, 11/11. The SharedWorker unit control uses actual page-side expressions and target-specific worker realms, then verifies release before navigation, iframe isolation, reattachment and last-window rejection.
- [First hosted probe](https://github.com/neomjs/neo/actions/runs/42529888246), `bd92f06c78`: 11/11 passed. The production log parser measured ResetSurvivesReload at 24.8 seconds and TopologyGroups at 64.3 seconds; only those two keys are added to the shard table.
- [Second hosted probe](https://github.com/neomjs/neo/actions/runs/42530476048), `10dae9ded4`: 11/11 passed with no skipped, failed or flaky tests. The only delta between the two probe heads is the two measured JSON duration entries; adapter and test bytes are identical.
- Integrated head `8e5796992f`: full local unit suite 6,676 passed / 2 skipped; [targeted hosted probe](https://github.com/neomjs/neo/actions/runs/42532991301) passed all 11 cases again. All adapter and test bytes match the approved `10dae9ded4` head.
- [Full engine run](https://github.com/neomjs/neo/actions/runs/42532916859) at that same head: attempt 1 passed the two admitted files but failed `NewsTabOverflow` once (missing Medium at 390×664). One unchanged-head retry of only shard 12 passed 39/39, including all three Portal overflow cases; all 14 shards are now green. No Portal source, assertion or timeout changed. The intermittent failure's cause remains unproven.

### 🧭 Patch-Blind Premise Snapshot

*   **Inputs Read Before Patch:** #20614's body (I wrote it), `dev`'s `runDedicatedWorkerNeuralLink` after #20615 (whose release hooks I wrote), `sharedWorkerAppWorker.mjs`, and the two cold-context specs' `coldRoot` / `connectToApp(await readWorkerId(page))` paths.
*   **Expected Solution Shape:** One binder per `Page`: the worker capture, the logs, the held SharedWorker session and both release hooks, memoized by page. `connectToApp(<UUID>)` finds the root page whose App Worker reports that id, in any context, and serves it through its own binder. A name target stays fixture-local. It must not hardcode an app name or a context, and it must never guess between candidates. Test isolation: a fake browser with several contexts, plus a wrong-id control.
*   **Patch Verdict:** Matches. `bindPage` (`dedicatedWorkerNeuralLink.mjs:665`) memoizes a binder per page, carrying its own `logs`, `appWorker` and `sharedAttach`, the document-route release and the last-window release. The last-window release now also covers sibling pages that were already open. The UUID scan skips closed pages and pages with an `opener()`. The readiness probe then re-checks `readyId === target` on the attached worker, so a scan match alone binds nothing. The SDK closes over `binding.getWorker` / `binding.getLogs`, so a later `connectToApp` cannot redirect an earlier SDK.
*   **Premise Coherence:** Coheres with verify-before-assert. The binding requires an exact UUID and re-proves it on the attached worker; a context is never picked by name or by guess.

### 🔬 Depth Floor

**Challenge OR documented search (per guide §7.1):**

- **Challenge**: `bindPage` memoizes the whole async initializer, which includes `await boundPage.route?.(…)`. If the target page closes between the poll's `isClosed()` check and that `route` call, the rejected promise stays in `bindings`. Teardown's `await (await binding).release()` (`:886`) then rethrows it, and the test reports a teardown error in place of its own result. The window is narrow, a page closing in the middle of `connectToApp`. Non-blocking. A one-line hardening can ride with the `dev` merge: drop the entry on rejection, and let teardown tolerate one (`await (await binding.catch(() => null))?.release()`).
